articles.title: We Updated Our Privacy Policy. Here's What Changed and Why.
articles.summary: Microsoft drops 167 security fixes including a SharePoint zero-day and the deliciously named 'BlueHammer' Windows Defender bug. AI is apparently better at finding vulns than humans now—great, our robot overlords can hack us before they enslave us.

articles.title: Anti-DDoS Firm Heaped Attacks on Brazilian ISPs
articles.summary: Canvas education platform gets ransomed by cybercriminals, disrupting schools nationwide with defaced login pages. Nothing says 'back to school' like having your homework held hostage by script kiddies.

articles.title: Pwn2Own Berlin 2026, Day Three: DEVCORE Crowned Master of Pwn, $1.298 Million Total
articles.summary: Microsoft Exchange Server zero-day being actively exploited via crafted emails with no permanent patch for on-prem deployments. Exchange strikes again—because apparently Microsoft's email server is as secure as a screen door on a submarine.

articles.title: Fuel Tank Breaches Expand Scope of Iran's Cyber Offensive
articles.summary: Instagram kills its end-to-end encryption feature after promising privacy protections for years. Meta breaks another promise to users—shocking absolutely no one who's been paying attention to Zuckerberg's track record.

articles.title: Poland directs officials to ditch Signal in favor of 'secure' state-developed alternative
articles.summary: 18-year-old NGINX Rift vulnerability already being exploited within days of disclosure. When your web server flaw is old enough to vote, you know someone's been sleeping at the security wheel.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds a flaw in Microsoft Exchange Server to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: Pwn2Own Berlin 2026 wraps with 47 zero-days discovered and $1.29M in payouts, DEVCORE taking the crown. Nothing like competitive hacking to remind vendors that their 'secure' products are Swiss cheese.

articles.title: Patch Tuesday, April 2026 Edition
articles.summary: Scattered Spider member 'Tylerb' pleads guilty to wire fraud and identity theft in SMS phishing campaign. Another cybercrime group member learns that prison orange clashes with their hacker aesthetic.

articles.title: Help EFF Solve an Issue That's Bigger than Creepy Ads
articles.summary: EFF releases guide to combat systematic surveillance abuses across the Americas. Because apparently we need step-by-step instructions to remind governments that mass surveillance isn't actually legal or cool.

articles.title: NGINX Rift attackers waste no time targeting exposed servers
articles.summary: Shai-Hulud worm exploits GitHub Actions to poison TanStack's shared cache in supply chain attack. Even our code repositories aren't safe from sandworms—Paul Atreides would be proud of this digital spice heist.

articles.title: Grafana GitHub Token Breach Led to Codebase Download and Extortion Attempt
articles.summary: Grafana rejects ransom demand after hackers steal source code via GitHub token compromise. At least someone still has a spine when extortionists come knocking—take notes, other breached companies.
